items.author: Nurbek Bekmurzaev
items.title: In Kyrgyzstan, public meetings with the president turn into a quest to seek justice
items.summary: The message is clear: People have lost all hope of finding justice at the hands of local police and courts.

items.author: Laura
items.title: Nigerien women lose their rights before ever reaching a courtroom
items.summary: Long before reaching any courtroom, women face barriers not only within their families and communities, but also in the resolution of disputes, often over land, inheritance, and child custody.

items.author: Susmita Aryal
items.title: Breaking the silence: Pratishta’s journey from childhood abuse to advocacy
items.summary: Across South Asia, including Nepal, survivors of rape and child sexual abuse face not only violence but also victim-blaming social norms that perpetuate stigma, silence and impunity.

items.author: Cynthia Ebot Takang
items.title: Growing up displaced in Cameroon after ten years of conflict
items.summary: In Buea, children displaced by Cameroon’s armed Anglophone conflict are balancing school with market trading to help their families survive, while years of displacement have interrupted their education, relationships, aspirations.

items.author: Sanjib Chaudhary
items.title: Reclaiming Indigenous culinary histories in Nepal
items.summary: Sanjib Chaudhary of Global Voices caught up with Binti Gurung, a food historian and founder of Natural Roots Foundation, to talk about her work on the food heritage of Nepal.

items.author: Sydney Allen
items.title: The ongoing efforts to get ecocide recognized at the International Criminal Court
items.summary: For the nations that started this, the stakes are not abstract. They are asking the world to build infrastructure to prosecute and prevent harm that is already happening to them.

items.author: Jo Carter
items.title: Why Japan’s anti-hate measures fall short
items.summary: The prevalence of online hate speech is to a large extent related to a lack of effective domestic legislation and human rights education.

items.author: Daria Dergacheva
items.title: Family stories keep alive Georgia’s democratic past and the memory of Soviet repression
items.summary: “Family stories can open up broader conversations about democracy, human rights, repression, and civic responsibility”

items.author: Daria Dergacheva
items.title: In Moldova, teens are learning about democracy and elections through an app
items.summary: VotEDU started off as a civic-education project to help young people understand democracy before they vote for the first time.

items.author: Global Voices Announcements
items.title: Support Global Voices’ December Spotlight: Digital Communities
items.summary: In this month’s spotlight, Global Voices, in partnership with Ranking Digital Rights, will explore the multiverse of digital communities — starting with our own.
